Description:
Family Day Care offers child care in a family home. This care is for more than three hours per day per child. It can include:

Three to six children, ages six weeks to 12 years
Plus two more school-age children
One staff member can care for:

Up to six children younger than school age
Eight children if at least two are school-aged
There must always be one caregiver for every two children under the age of two.

Group Family Day Care is child care in a family home on a regular basis. It lasts more than three hours per day per child. This care can include:

Seven to 12 children, ages six weeks to 12 years
Four more school-age children
A primary on-site provider runs a Group Family Day Care.

Caregiver requirements
One caregiver can care for up to six children younger than school age.
They can care for eight children if at least two of them are school-aged.
Two caregivers must be present when more than six children, none of whom are school age, are in care.
There must be at least one caregiver for every two children under the age of two years.

Center-Based Day Care offers childcare for 3+ kids under six years of age. Center-based childcare prorams are run out of non-home facilities. This care is for more than five hours per week per child, for at least 30+ days per year
Create an ID with the NYC Health Department (routine identification information).
Attend a pre-permit orientation session at your local Borough Office to receive a completion certificate number.

Step: Alarm System and Sprinkler System installation
Description: Install alarm and sprinkler systems (if required, following specific city requirements) previously approved by FDNY.
Ensure facility has proper emergency safety plan.
Obtain DOB certification for site renovations/changes. This assumes possession of official architectural plans for the facility.
Obtain FDNY approval for site renovations/construction. Requirements vary by building specifics.
Obtain a private provider to verify that the facility's water supply is not contaminated,
Submit an application for lead paint testing to your Local Borough Office of DOHMH.
Obtain a private provider to verify that the soil outside/around your facility is not contaminated
Ensure building passes all site requirements and make changes if necessary.
Fill out application for site viability inspection by a city employee.
Ensure all staff members have necessary immunizations and have provided medical records from the last 2 years.
Obtain fingerprints for all staff members at DOHMH's IdenToGo fingerprint locations.
Ensure all staff members obtain the necessary clearance of criminal history and the Statewide Central Register of Child Abuse and Maltreatment.

Step: Ensure all staff have proper trainings
Description: Ensure that all groups of children are properly monitored by sufficiently-trained staff.
Verify that all extraneous requirements in policy and facility guidelines are being followed.
Obtain Food Protection Certificate for at least one supervising manager.
Complete online application using all previous documents, certificates, etc.
Create an account on the Aspire Registry to be accessible alongside all other Group Child Care facilities.

Step: Complete the Child Day Care Orientation
Description: Log-in to New York State Office of Child and Family Services portal to complete.
After completing orientation, request an application in New York State Office of Child and Family Services portal. .

Once your application has been submitted and reviewed, a representative from OCFS will complete an inspection.  If your daycare business is approved, then a license or registration will be mailed to you

Step: Contact a Regional Office or Child Care Resource and Referral (CCRR) agency
Description: OCFS Regional Offices can provide application materials and information about the process of starting a program. Child Care Resource and Referral Agencies (CCRR) also provide start-up information and information on funding eligibility.

Step: Attend pre-licensing Health and Safety Training
Description: To ensure that new providers are prepared for this responsibility, they must complete health and safety training approved by the Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS).

Step: Complete and submit blackground check and fingerprinting
Description: To initiate the comprehensive background check process, individuals must follow the instructions on the OCFS-4930 form to schedule a fingerprinting appointment and also submit a completed OCFS-6000 packet to their program’s provider/director. For staff who have already been fingerprinted for day care under the CCDBG requirements and have not had a break in service for more than 180 days, you will complete the Request for a Waiver to initiate the process.

CCDBG Background Checks | Division of Child Care Services
OCFS-4930
OCFS-6000
Waiver if previously fingerprinted

Description: Complete 30 hours of training in ten topic areas every two years. You must finish 15 of these hours within the first six months of employment.

Step: Complete Foundations in Health and Safety e-learning
Description:
5-hour e-learning course “Foundations in Health and Safety.” Required pre-service or within three (3) months of start date.
 or
15-hour classroom training “Health and Safety: Competencies for Becoming a Family or Group Family Day Care Provider.“ Required pre-service or within three (3) months of start date.

Step: Arrange CPR and First Aid certification
Description: Each program must have at least one (1) person on site who is certified in CPR/First Aid during all hours of operation.
Optional except for programs that choose to administer medications or as otherwise required.

The initial registration period for a Family Day Care program is two years.
After that, the renewal registration is effective for four years.
Providers must follow the Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS) regulations and all laws that apply.
